text: As a body bred to a good habit requires nothing exquisite either in clothes or food, so a sound man and a sound household keep themselves up with a small matter. Riches ought to be proportioned to the use we have of them; for he that scrapes together a great deal, making use of but little, is not independent; for if he wants them not, it is folly in him to make provision for things which he does not desire; or if he does desire them, and restrains his enjoyment out of sordidness, he is miserable.
author: Plutarch
locator: Comparison of Aristides with Marcus Cato
translation: John Dryden et al., rev. Arthur Hugh Clough, 1864
